findings.title: Timeout remediation claim is false — Task 14's assertion cannot pass as written
findings.description: Task 13 states the timeout rejection should "run through the existing `withNetworkErrorHint` path so the remediation text is appended (the `/timed out/i` pattern already matches)", and Task 14 asserts the rejection message contains `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION`. The actual `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS` list has `/connection timed out/i` and `/etimedout/i` — there is no bare `/timed out/i` pattern. A message phrased as Task 13 requires ("the git command timed out after N seconds") matches neither pattern, so `withNetworkErrorHint` returns it unchanged and `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` is absent. A junior AI following Task 13 verbatim produces code that fails Task 14's success criteria. Fix by adding a `/timed out/i` pattern in Task 13's step list (a small scope addition no task currently authorizes), or by changing Task 14 to assert the timeout message only and adding a separate assertion for the hint. Note the slice design makes the same incorrect claim ("`/timed out/i` is in `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS`"), so the design is wrong here, not just the task.

findings.title: `detect()` throwing on `'error'` breaks existing `GuideDetector` submodule tests, and no task updates them
findings.description: Task 11 makes `detect()` call `checkSyncStatus()` for submodule installs and throw when it returns `'error'`. Three existing tests in `GuideDetector.test.ts` ("detects submodule even when .git/ also exists", "detects submodule method when .gitmodules contains path", "uses operationPath for guidePath when provided") stub `gitExec` to reject for anything other than `describe`/`ls-remote`; the new `['submodule','status', …]` call therefore hits the rejecting default and `detect()` throws where those tests expect a resolved `GuideInfo`. Task 4 only updates `manual`→`tarball` expectations, and Task 12 adds new checkout cases without mentioning these three. The tasks need an explicit step to give those tests a `submodule status` response.

findings.title: `GuideInfo.checkout` is added as a required field mid-sequence with no task owning the fallout
findings.description: Task 10 adds `checkout: SubmoduleCheckoutState | null` to `GuideInfo` and its own success criterion is "typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field" — i.e. it knowingly leaves core non-typechecking between Task 10 and Task 11. Worse, the existing fixtures annotated as `GuideInfo` in `GuideManager.test.ts` (`notInstalledInfo`, `installedInfo`) will fail `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core typecheck` until a `checkout` value is added, and no task lists that edit — Task 18 touches that file but only to add `ensureCheckout()` cases. Either make the field optional in Task 10 or add the fixture update to Task 10/11 explicitly. (`packages/cli/tests/commands/guides.test.ts` and `packages/mcp-server/tests/guideTools.test.ts` use untyped fixtures, so they are unaffected.)

findings.title: Real-git fixture tests are placed in files that mock the modules under test
findings.description: Task 18 puts the `cloned()`/`initialized()`/`out_of_sync()` assertions (real directory populated, 7+ char commit, `git submodule status` unchanged) in `GuideManager.test.ts`, which mocks `fs`, `../../src/guides/gitExec.js`, `GuideDetector`, and all three strategy modules — including `SubmoduleStrategy`. As written the test cannot exercise the real `init()`/`detect()` path. Task 21 has the same shape at the CLI layer: `build.test.ts` mocks the entire `@context-forge/core/node` barrel (`FileProjectStore`, `createContextPipeline`, `ConfigManager`), so the `GuideManager` that Task 19's `ensureGuideReady()` builds would be the mock, not the real class. Both tasks need a stated approach (partial `importActual` mock, or a new test file that does not stub core), otherwise the fixture work of Task 9 yields tests that assert nothing about the auto-init behavior.

findings.title: MCP wiring point leaks auto-init into `template_preview`, which declares itself side-effect free
findings.description: Task 22 says to call `ensureCheckout()` "before `createContextPipeline` (~line 57)". Line 57 is inside the shared `generateContext()` helper, which is used by `context_build`, `template_preview` (line ~220) and `prompt_*`. `template_preview` is registered with `readOnlyHint: true` and a description promising it runs "without triggering any side effects"; auto-initializing a submodule there contradicts both, and the design's D3 list covers only `context_build`/`prompt_list`/`prompt_get`. The task must say where the call goes so `template_preview` is excluded (or the design's exclusion list is deliberately amended).

findings.title: Rename-verification greps miss the user-facing `manual` strings they are meant to retire
findings.description: Task 3's success criterion is `grep -rn "'manual'" packages/core/src` returning only the alias entry and the `ConfigKeys` enum line. The remaining non-alias occurrences — `CloneStrategy.ts:34` and `SubmoduleStrategy.ts:39,45` ("use the `"manual"` strategy instead", "--strategy clone or --strategy manual instead") plus the comment at `GuideManager.ts:135` — are double-quoted or unquoted, so the single-quote grep passes while user-facing advice still names a deprecated alias. The design's "Rename sweep (exact locations)" does list those line numbers and Task 3 names those files, so the work is in scope; only the verification is too weak. Use a quote-agnostic grep for the success criterion.

findings.title: Several effort-1 fragments could merge without losing anything
findings.description: Task count (32) is defensible for a five-part slice touching ~10 source files plus docs, and no step dictates implementation detail the design does not require. But Tasks 13+14 (gitExec timeout + its single test), Task 24 (one `Checkout:` line + its test), and Task 25 (descriptor + help text, whose consumer Task 26 adds immediately after) are fragments that each trigger a full build/test cycle for a few lines. Merging 13+14 and 24 into the neighbouring task would cut three commit/verification cycles. Not blocking — the file is not overweight overall, and the test-with pattern is respected everywhere.

findings.title: Task 27's first-named test file cannot cover the help output it asserts
findings.description: Task 27 says "`help.test.ts` (or `guides.test.ts`): both `--help` outputs contain `submodule`, `clone`, and `tarball`". `help.test.ts` builds a synthetic `Command` program with hand-registered `build`/`list`/`slice`/`concept` commands and never calls `registerInitCommand`/`registerGuidesCommand`, so it cannot observe either help string. The parenthetical hedge saves the task, but naming an unusable file first invites a wasted attempt — point at `guides.test.ts` (or a new test registering both commands).
